advances: The two inner supports give exact mixed-cap capacities only when the corresponding inner and outer lines converge; the parallel and diverging cases give no finite capacity.  On the finite branch, the two supports also give a sharp closed formula for the southwest hull defect.  Nevertheless, the resulting slope-cap, defect-anchor, support-polygon-area, and boundary-complete chord system does not imply the requested aspect bound.  An exact rational tuple satisfies all of those scalar inequalities, with both cap bounds and both chord-order comparisons at equality, but has support-polygon ratio \(18>5000/291\).  The first omitted actual-body constraint is the area of the simultaneous outer-support envelope: the exact strongest outer coefficients must constrain \(\operatorname{conv}(0,P)\), not merely the two caps.  The rational tuple violates that envelope inequality and hence is not an Alternative 1 body.
author: mp_r111_regime_a_slope_elimination
proof:
The zero southwest cell in accepted fact `bc026780453747b8` and convexity imply that \(A_0\) has no point in the open southwest quadrant.  Otherwise, mixing such a point with an interior point produces an open southwest subset of \(A_0\), contradicting zero southwest area.  If \(b=0<a\), then \((0,0)\) lies in the body, so the segment from \((0,0)\) to \((a,0)\), followed by \([a,A]\times\{0\}\), makes the full horizontal trace \([0,A]\times\{0\}\) of length \(a+1>1\).  If \(a=0<b\), the coordinate-swapped argument makes the full vertical trace \(\{0\}\times[0,B]\) of length \(b+1>1\).  Hence exactly one zero offset is impossible.

At the boundary point \((a,0)\), choose a supporting line and orient its normal so that the body is in its nonnegative halfplane.  The segment from \((a,0)\) to \((A,0)\) makes the first normal coordinate nonnegative.  Positive lower mixed-cell area rules out a zero first coordinate.  The point \((0,b)\), together with \(a,b>0\), then makes the second normal coordinate positive.  Dividing the normal by its second coordinate gives the first inequality in (1) with \(0<\sigma<\infty\).  The coordinate-swapped argument at \((0,b)\) gives the second inequality with \(0<\rho<\infty\).  When \(a=b=0\), a supporting line at the common origin exists; the two positive axis traces make both normal coordinates nonnegative, and the two positive mixed cells rule out either being zero.  The same line may be used for both roles, or two different supporting lines may be chosen when the support cone is nontrivial.  No division by \(a\) or \(b\) is involved.

Substitution of \((0,b)\) and \((a,0)\) into (1) gives (2).  Multiplication gives \(\sigma\rho\leq1\).  If equality holds, both inequalities in (2) must be equalities, which proves the incidence assertion preceding (10).

Take a lower-cap point \((x,y)\) with \(y<0\), and take \((u,v)\in P\) with \(v>0\).  Their segment meets the \(x\)-axis at
\[
\left(\frac{vx-yu}{v-y},0\right).
\]
This point lies in the full trace \([a,A]\times\{0\}\), so its abscissa is at most \(A\).  Since \(v-y>0\), this is exactly
\[
v(x-A)\leq y(u-A),
\qquad
x-A\leq\frac{u-A}{v}\,y.                                 \tag{23}
\]
A fixed lower-cap point bounds all ratios in (4) from above after division by the negative number \(y\), proving that \(\alpha\) is finite.  Taking the supremum in (23), with \(y<0\), gives
\[
x-A\leq\alpha y.                                         \tag{24}
\]
At depth \(t=-y\geq0\), the first inner support in (1) and (24) give
\[
a+\frac t\sigma\leq x\leq A-\alpha t.                    \tag{25}
\]
The interval in (25) has length \(1-q_xt\).  If \(q_x>0\), it vanishes at \(t=1/q_x\), and integration gives
\[
\int_0^{1/q_x}(1-q_xt)\,dt=\frac1{2q_x}.
\]
This proves (6).  If \(q_x=0\), (25) is a constant-width unbounded strip; if \(q_x<0\), its width increases with \(t\).  This proves all lower-cap cases, including \(\alpha=0\).

For a left-cap point \((x,y)\) with \(x<0\), and a positive-cell point \((u,v)\) with \(u>0\), the \(y\)-axis intercept of their segment is
\[
\left(0,\frac{uy-xv}{u-x}\right).
\]
It is at most \(B\), so
\[
u(y-B)\leq x(v-B).
\]
Taking the strongest coefficient gives
\[
y-B\leq\beta x.
\]
Writing \(t=-x\geq0\), the second inner support in (1) gives the vertical interval
\[
b+\frac t\rho\leq y\leq B-\beta t,
\]
of length \(1-q_yt\).  The preceding integration proves (7) and all its parallel, diverging, and zero-coefficient cases.

For the defect calculation, let
\[
\Delta=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(a,0),(0,b)\}.
\]
The two trace endpoints belong to \(P\), so \(\Delta\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(0,P)\).  Equation (1) implies
\[
P\cap\Delta\subseteq
\Delta\cap\{y+\sigma(x-a)\geq0\}
\cap\{x+\rho(y-b)\geq0\}.                                \tag{26}
\]
When \(\sigma\rho<1\), the two support lines meet at
\[
S=
\left(
\frac{\rho(b-\sigma a)}{1-\sigma\rho},
\frac{\sigma(a-\rho b)}{1-\sigma\rho}
\right).                                                  \tag{27}
\]
Conditions (2) put \(S\) in \(\Delta\).  The allowed part on the right of (26) is the triangle with vertices \((a,0),(0,b),S\).  Its area is
\[
\frac{(b-\sigma a)(a-\rho b)}
     {2(1-\sigma\rho)}.
\]
Subtracting this from \(|\Delta|=ab/2\) proves (8)-(9).  The bound is sharp because equality is attained when the southwest part of \(P\) is exactly that triangle.  When \(\sigma\rho=1\), the support lines coincide with the trace-endpoint chord, so the allowed part of \(\Delta\) has area zero and (10) follows.  The case \(a=b=0\) is immediate from \(|\Delta|=0\).

Accepted fact `92a1b537d7e7876c` gives
\[
D|\operatorname{conv}(0,P)|\leq\frac9{200r_-^2}.
\]
Subtracting \(D|P|=p\), supplied by accepted fact `bc026780453747b8`, proves (11).  Rationalizing
\[
\frac1{r_-}=\frac{29+\sqrt{65}}6
\]
gives the displayed exact value of \(k\).

Shoelace gives (12).  Horizontal section length in a polygon is affine between consecutive vertex levels.  If \(b\leq Y\), the section at \(y=Y\) runs from \(x=0\) to \(x=W\), proving (14).  If \(Y<b\), the ordered levels are
\[
0\leq Y<b<B\leq H.
\]
The section at \(y=Y\) has length
\[
W-a\frac{b-Y}{b}=G_x,
\]
and the section at \(y=b\) has length
\[
W-(W-X)\frac{b-Y}{H-Y}=J_x.
\]
The length at \(y=0\) is \(1\leq G_x\), the length at \(y=B\) is at most \(J_x\), and the remaining vertex levels are no larger.  This proves (15), including the tie \(G_x=J_x\).  Exchanging the coordinates proves (16)-(17).  The weak first branches contain \(Y=b\) and \(X=a\), and the strict second branches have nonzero denominators, so all level-order boundary strata are covered.

It remains to verify the obstruction.  For (20), (2) reads
\[
8\geq4,\qquad 8\geq4,
\]
and \(\sigma\rho=1/4<1\).  Formula (8) gives
\[
\Phi
=
\frac{(1/2)64+(1/2)64-2(1/4)64}
     {2(3/4)}
=\frac{64}{3}
=E.                                                       \tag{28}
\]
The support polygon is
\[
K=\operatorname{conv}\{(8,0),(9,0),(0,9),(0,8)\}.
\]
Every point \((u,v)\in K\) with \(v>0\) satisfies \(u+v\leq9\), with equality on the outer edge.  Hence
\[
\alpha_K=\sup_{v>0}\frac{u-9}{v}=-1.
\]
The coordinate-swapped supremum is also \(\beta_K=-1\), so (20) satisfies (13a) at equality.  Thus \(q_x=q_y=1\), and
\[
\frac cD=\frac{3/200}{3/100}=\frac12
=\frac1{2q_x}=\frac1{2q_y}.                              \tag{29}
\]
Both cap capacities are attained.

Equation (12) gives \(T=17/2\), so
\[
DT=\frac{51}{200}<\frac{97}{100}=p.                      \tag{30}
\]
Also
\[
T+\frac{ab}{2}-\frac pD
=\frac{81}{2}-\frac{97}{3}
=\frac{49}{6}
<\frac{64}{3}=E.                                         \tag{31}
\]
The defect anchor is
\[
DE=\frac3{100}\frac{64}{3}=\frac{16}{25}
<
\frac{65+29\sqrt{65}}{400}=k,                            \tag{32}
\]
because \(29\sqrt{65}>191\), as follows after squaring from
\[
29^2\cdot65=54665>36481=191^2.
\]
Even the stronger support-polygon anchor retained in (18) holds:
\[
D\left(T+\frac{ab}{2}\right)
=\frac3{100}\frac{81}{2}
=\frac{243}{200}
<
\frac{453+29\sqrt{65}}{400}
=\frac9{200r_-^2}.                                       \tag{33}
\]

Here \(Y=0<b\) and \(X=0<a\).  Equations (15) and (17) give
\[
G_x=J_x=G_y=J_y=1.
\]
Thus all four section-order comparisons are ties, \(M_x=M_y=1\), and (21) follows because
\[
18\cdot291=5238>5000.
\]

Finally, an actual \(P\) with the exact coefficients \(\alpha=\beta=-1\) must obey \(x+y\leq9\).  The origin obeys the same inequality, so
\[
\operatorname{conv}(0,P)\subseteq
\{x,y\geq0:x+y\leq9\}.
\]
This proves (22) for the tuple.  But
\[
\frac pD+E=\frac{97}{3}+\frac{64}{3}=\frac{161}{3}
>\frac{81}{2}.
\]
Equivalently, the two inner supports remove the area \(64/3\) from the outer triangle, leaving only
\[
\frac{81}{2}-\frac{64}{3}=\frac{115}{6}
<\frac{97}{3}=\frac pD.
\]
Therefore no positive cell realizes all scalar entries in (20).  The missing condition is exactly the simultaneous inner/outer support-envelope area constraint, not another cap inequality.
statement:
Assume the complete Alternative 1 hypotheses of accepted facts `bc026780453747b8` and `92a1b537d7e7876c`.  Normalize the full positive axis traces of \(P\) to
\[
[a,A]\times\{0\},\qquad \{0\}\times[b,B],
\qquad A=a+1,\quad B=b+1,
\]
and let \(D>0\) be the product of the two physical trace lengths.  Thus
\[
|P|=\frac pD,\qquad p=\frac{97}{100},
\]
and each normalized mixed cap of \(A_0\) has area
\[
\frac cD,\qquad c=\frac3{200}.
\]

There are finite positive numbers \(\sigma,\rho\) for which the full normalized \(A_0\) body obeys the division-free supporting inequalities
\[
y+\sigma(x-a)\geq0,\qquad
x+\rho(y-b)\geq0.                                      \tag{1}
\]
The first support passes through \((a,0)\), and the second passes through \((0,b)\).  An actual normalized trace has either \(a,b>0\), or \(a=b=0\).  In the first case,
\[
b\geq\sigma a,\qquad a\geq\rho b,\qquad \sigma\rho\leq1. \tag{2}
\]

Define the exact strongest outer coefficients without assuming that a maximizing point exists:
\[
\alpha=\inf\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:
u-A\leq\lambda v\ \hbox{for every }(u,v)\in P\},
\]
\[
\beta=\inf\{\lambda\in\mathbb R:
v-B\leq\lambda u\ \hbox{for every }(u,v)\in P\}.          \tag{3}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\alpha=\sup_{\substack{(u,v)\in P\\v>0}}\frac{u-A}{v},
\qquad
\beta=\sup_{\substack{(u,v)\in P\\u>0}}\frac{v-B}{u}.     \tag{4}
\]
Both numbers are finite.  Put
\[
q_x=\alpha+\frac1\sigma,\qquad
q_y=\beta+\frac1\rho.                                    \tag{5}
\]
If \(q_x>0\), the normalized lower cap is contained in a triangle of area \(1/(2q_x)\), and hence
\[
D\geq2cq_x=\frac3{100}q_x.                               \tag{6}
\]
If \(q_x=0\), the two relevant lines are parallel and cut out an unbounded strip of width one.  If \(q_x<0\), they cut out an expanding unbounded wedge.  Thus (1) and (3) alone give no finite lower-cap capacity in those two cases.  The coordinate-swapped statement is exact: if \(q_y>0\), then
\[
D\geq2cq_y=\frac3{100}q_y,                               \tag{7}
\]
whereas \(q_y=0\) and \(q_y<0\) give respectively an unbounded strip and an expanding wedge.  In particular, a zero outer coefficient causes no singularity: \(\alpha=0\) gives lower-cap capacity \(\sigma/2\), and \(\beta=0\) gives left-cap capacity \(\rho/2\).

Let
\[
E=|\operatorname{conv}(0,P)|-|P|.
\]
If \(a,b>0\) and \(\sigma\rho<1\), define
\[
\Phi(a,b,\sigma,\rho)
=
\frac{\sigma a^2+\rho b^2-2\sigma\rho ab}
     {2(1-\sigma\rho)}
=
\frac{ab}{2}
-
\frac{(b-\sigma a)(a-\rho b)}
     {2(1-\sigma\rho)}.                                  \tag{8}
\]
Then the sharp support-line defect bound is
\[
E\geq\Phi(a,b,\sigma,\rho).                              \tag{9}
\]
If \(a,b>0\) and \(\sigma\rho=1\), (2) forces
\[
b=\sigma a,\qquad a=\rho b;
\]
the two support lines coincide with the line through the inner trace endpoints, and the sharp bound is
\[
E\geq\frac{ab}{2}.                                       \tag{10}
\]
If \(a=b=0\), the southwest trace triangle is degenerate and the sharp bound is \(E\geq0\), regardless of whether the two chosen support lines coincide.  Exactly one zero offset is impossible for an actual normalized trace.

Accepted fact `92a1b537d7e7876c`, together with \(|P|=p/D\) from accepted fact `bc026780453747b8`, gives
\[
DE\leq k,\qquad
k=\frac9{200r_-^2}-p
=\frac{65+29\sqrt{65}}{400},
\qquad
r_-=\frac{87-3\sqrt{65}}{388}.                           \tag{11}
\]

For the fully inward support polygon
\[
K=\operatorname{conv}\{(a,0),(A,0),(W,Y),(X,H),(0,B),(0,b)\},
\]
assume
\[
0\leq X\leq A\leq W,\qquad
0\leq Y\leq B\leq H,
\]
and \((W,Y)\ne(X,H)\).  Its area is
\[
T=|K|=\frac{AY+WH-XY+XB-ab}{2}.                          \tag{12}
\]
Since \(K\subseteq P\),
\[
DT\leq p.                                                 \tag{13}
\]
Put
\[
\alpha_K=\sup_{\substack{(u,v)\in K\\v>0}}\frac{u-A}{v},
\qquad
\beta_K=\sup_{\substack{(u,v)\in K\\u>0}}\frac{v-B}{u}.
\]
The exact coefficients in (4) necessarily satisfy
\[
\alpha\geq\alpha_K,\qquad \beta\geq\beta_K.               \tag{13a}
\]
Its exact maximum horizontal chord \(M_x=m_x(K)\) is
\[
M_x=W\quad\hbox{if }b\leq Y,                              \tag{14}
\]
whereas, if \(Y<b\), then \(b>0\), \(H>Y\), and
\[
G_x=W-\frac{a(b-Y)}b,\qquad
J_x=W-\frac{(W-X)(b-Y)}{H-Y},
\qquad
M_x=\max\{G_x,J_x\}.                                     \tag{15}
\]
The exact maximum vertical chord \(M_y=m_y(K)\) is
\[
M_y=H\quad\hbox{if }a\leq X,                              \tag{16}
\]
whereas, if \(X<a\), then \(a>0\), \(W>X\), and
\[
G_y=H-\frac{b(a-X)}a,\qquad
J_y=H-\frac{(H-Y)(a-X)}{W-X},
\qquad
M_y=\max\{G_y,J_y\}.                                     \tag{17}
\]
Equations (14)-(17) include \(Y=b\), \(X=a\), \(Y=0<b\), \(X=0<a\), both maximum ties, coincident outer trace endpoints, and nonunique support faces.

The scalar relaxation obtained by retaining from (3)-(4) only (13a), and otherwise consisting of (2), (5)-(17) and the elementary containment inequalities
\[
E\geq T+\frac{ab}{2}-\frac pD,\qquad
D\left(T+\frac{ab}{2}\right)\leq\frac9{200r_-^2}          \tag{18}
\]
does not imply
\[
\frac W{M_x}+\frac H{M_y}\leq\frac{5000}{291}.            \tag{19}
\]
Indeed, the following tuple is an exact rational obstruction:
\[
a=b=8,\quad A=B=W=H=9,\quad X=Y=0,
\]
\[
\sigma=\rho=\frac12,\quad
\alpha=\beta=-1,\quad
D=\frac3{100},\quad
E=\frac{64}{3}.                                          \tag{20}
\]
It lies in the strictly finite branch \(q_x=q_y=1\), satisfies every displayed scalar inequality, and gives
\[
M_x=M_y=1,\qquad
\frac W{M_x}+\frac H{M_y}=18>\frac{5000}{291}.            \tag{21}
\]

The first missing actual-body constraint is
\[
\frac pD+E
=|\operatorname{conv}(0,P)|
\leq
\left|
\{(x,y)\in[0,W]\times[0,H]:
x-A\leq\alpha y,\ y-B\leq\beta x\}
\right|.                                                  \tag{22}
\]
For (20), the set on the right of (22) is the triangle
\[
\{x,y\geq0:x+y\leq9\}
\]
of area \(81/2\), whereas the left side is \(161/3\).  Equivalently, intersecting that outer triangle with the two inner halfplanes in (1) gives maximum possible positive-cell area \(115/6\), while (20) requires \(|P|=p/D=97/3\).  Thus (20) is a counterexample to the requested slope-aware scalar elimination, not to the unchanged Alternative 1 theorem.
